prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key policies and commitments (2019 manifesto)

- EU and constitutional: Seek to remain in the EU by revoking Article 50 if winning a majority; otherwise pursue a referendum with an option to remain. Protect freedom of movement, expand voting rights for long-term EU residents, and reform electoral registration. Introduce proportional representation (STV), votes at 16, automatic voter registration, House of Lords reform, and a written federal constitution with further devolution across the UK.

- Economy and tax: Invest £130bn in infrastructure (transport, energy, schools, hospitals, housing, fibre broadband). Create a Green Investment Bank (£5bn initial capital). Raise R&D to 3% of GDP; expand catapults and regional innovation. Support SMEs (start-up allowance, prompt payment enforcement, expand British Business Bank). Reform company governance (employee board reps, purpose and due-diligence duties). Tax: restore corporation tax to 20%; replace business rates with a commercial landowner levy; align capital gains and income treatment; strengthen anti-avoidance; improve Digital Services Tax.

- Skills and work: £10,000 lifetime Skills Wallet per adult; expand and refocus apprenticeships; flexible working from day one; new “dependent contractor” status with basic rights; right to request fixed hours; stronger enforcement; strengthen union access.

- Education and childcare: Free, high-quality childcare 35 hours/week for 48 weeks from 9 months for working parents, and for all 2–4-year-olds; increase funding to schools and hire 20,000 teachers; scrap SATs and league tables, replace Ofsted; expand SEND funding; boost FE funding (+£1bn), restore maintenance grants; student mental health charter.

- Climate and environment: Net zero by 2045; at least 80% electricity from renewables by 2030; ban fracking; insulate homes and end fuel poverty by 2025; zero‑carbon new buildings (from 2021; tighter by 2025); all new cars/vans electric by 2030; rail network ultra‑low‑emission by 2035; Clean Air Act; plant 60m trees/year; Nature Act; Zero‑Waste & Resource Efficiency Act (plastics bans, repairability, deposit return, 70% recycling target); expand protected land and marine areas; £5bn flood resilience fund.

- Transport: Freeze commuter rail fares for a parliament; reopen lines/stations; support HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, Crossrail 2 with tighter controls; new Railways Agency; extend ultra-low emission zones; shift freight to rail; invest in buses, trams, cycling and walking.

- Health and social care: Add 1p to Income Tax to raise £7bn/year ringfenced; £10bn capital; develop a dedicated Health and Care Tax; integrate health and care budgets. Mental health: new waiting time standards, expand talking therapies, 24/7 crisis care, perinatal support, free prescriptions for chronic conditions. Workforce plan, more GPs, targeted nursing bursaries. Public health: obesity, smoking levy, minimum unit pricing for alcohol, air quality law. Drug policy: divert possession to treatment; regulated cannabis market. Reproductive health: decriminalise abortion UK‑wide; clinic buffer zones.

- Social security and housing: Reduce first Universal Credit payment wait to 5 days; remove two‑child limit and benefit cap; increase work allowances; reform disability assessments; reinstate Independent Living Fund; overhaul bereavement support. Pensions: retain triple lock; address notification failures affecting certain cohorts. Housing: build 300,000 homes/year including 100,000 social; zero‑carbon standards; Rent to Own; longer tenancies; licensing and stronger standards; end rough sleeping within five years and repeal Vagrancy Act.

- Communities, policing and justice: £1bn for community policing; public‑health approach to violence; £500m for youth services; Online Crime Agency; domestic abuse measures; reduce disproportionate stop and search. Justice: presumption against short sentences; end imprisonment for possession for personal use; expand rehabilitation; reduce racial disparities; Women’s Justice Board.

- Immigration and asylum: End hostile environment; 28‑day detention limit; independent processing agency; flexible work visas; 2‑year post‑study work; lower/waive fees in key cases; right to work for asylum seekers after 3 months; expand resettlement and family reunion; improve decision‑making; English lessons; extend move‑on period.

- Foreign, defence, development, global climate: Maintain 0.7% aid; tighten arms export controls (suspend to Saudi Arabia); Magnitsky-style sanctions; NATO 2% GDP; cyber capability; maintain minimum nuclear deterrent with reduced posture; back Iran deal, recognise Palestine, support multilateral climate action (plastics treaty, biodiversity targets), end global fossil fuel subsidies.
